story.title: Story 1: Project Artifact Association Without Process Ownership

planSummary: Realigned project artifact association around current process refs and project-scoped shell summaries by removing legacy ownership implications from shell reads, deriving current-material artifact roles from revision provenance instead of artifact-row ownership hints, and allowing referenced artifacts to remain reviewable without regressing existing produced-artifact and package review flows.

changedFiles.reason: Derives process artifact role labels from artifact version provenance so current materials reflect current refs instead of legacy artifact ownership hints.
Expands review target eligibility to include current process refs while preserving existing produced-artifact and package review visibility.
Allows artifact review when the process currently references the artifact, while keeping prior produced-artifact access intact.
Adds coverage that project-shell artifact summaries strip legacy process ownership fields from API output.
Adds coverage for referenced-artifact materials labeling and review availability from current refs.
Adds coverage for reviewing an artifact referenced by a later process but produced by an earlier one.

findingsFixed: Replaced legacy ownership-dependent current-material role labeling with version-provenance-based labeling so real Convex artifact summaries no longer misclassify referenced artifacts.
Expanded review target and artifact review eligibility to include current refs without regressing existing produced-artifact and package-snapshot review behavior.
Caught and fixed the temporary integration regression caused by an overly narrow current-ref-only reviewability rule before final gate verification.

recommendedNextStep: Move to verification with focused checks on cross-process artifact reference behavior across the project shell, process materials, and review entry paths.
